description: Make reasoning effort a first-class execution configuration: a canonical reasoningEffort vocabulary on every write surface, the frozen (runtime, model, reasoningEffort, variant) + capabilityRevision tuple in all durable snapshots, versioned runtime catalog evidence separating variants from efforts, a pure typed-disposition resolver gating admission behind a claim-time capability fence, runtime-private native translation (Pi thinking level; OpenCode explicit unsupported), readiness/evidence/Web/CLI surfacing, and the deliberate removal of the Pi variant/thinking-level smuggling with no compatibility layer.

tasks.title: Canonical reasoningEffort write surface: AgentConfigSchema, issue override, and CLI
tasks.description: Add the canonical `reasoningEffort` vocabulary (`off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max` or unset) as an ordinary string-or-null key in `AgentConfigSchema`, accepted by both the Agent-definition surface (`AllowedKeys`) and the issue-level override (`IssueAllowedKeys`), with a shared `CanonicalReasoningEfforts` set and `ValidateReasoningEffort` helper so API, Web, and CLI use one list. Extend `mo agent create/update/view` with `--reasoning-effort` and mutually exclusive `--clear-reasoning-effort` (local validation against the canonical set, `ValidateClearSetPair` pattern, table rendering). The issue write-side merge paths (`IssueVariableBuilder`, `ConfigService`) pick the key up automatically via `IssueAllowedKeys`; `runtime` stays Agent-owned.
acceptanceCriteria: `agentConfig.reasoningEffort` accepts each of `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` and persists verbatim; a value outside the set (e.g. `extreme`) is rejected with an error naming all accepted values and nothing partial is persisted.
Wrong type, empty string, or non-null-non-string values are rejected under the same string-or-null, non-empty rules as `model` and `variant`; omitted or null effort is accepted.
Effort and variant stay independent: a config with both `reasoningEffort: high` and `variant: balanced` keeps both in separate fields, neither derived from or validated against the other.

The issue-level `agentConfig` override accepts `reasoningEffort` beside `model` and `variant` while still rejecting the Agent-owned `runtime` key, and the stored issue profile forwards the effort into the `vars.agent` execution options consumed by workflow agent tasks.

`mo agent create --reasoning-effort high` persists the effort and `mo agent view` renders it; `mo agent update --clear-reasoning-effort` removes only the effort key; passing both effort flags fails with a usage error; an invalid value is rejected locally before any request, listing accepted values.

Server schema tests cover the canonical set, wrong type/empty rejection, effort/variant independence, unset validity, and both write surfaces; CLI tests cover create/update/clear/view and local validation; relevant Server and CLI tests pass.
tasks.output: Canonical effort vocabulary and validation in AgentConfigSchema, issue-surface acceptance with vars.agent forwarding, CLI effort flags and view rendering, with passing schema and CLI tests.
tasks.notes: Design D1 + the CLI slice of D8. Also satisfies the requirements 'Canonical reasoning-effort vocabulary' and 'CLI exposes the effort on agent create, update, and view'. Keep the error message style mirroring the existing `runtime` message (names all accepted values). No write-time validation against a runner catalog — canonical-set validation only.

tasks.title: Freeze the effort tuple in every durable execution snapshot across all launch paths
tasks.description: Resolve and freeze `reasoningEffort` exactly like `variant` on every launch path: `AgentLauncher.ResolveReasoningEffort` feeding the `AgentExecutionSnapshot` composition; append-only record fields on `AgentExecutionDefinition` (Id 6), `AgentJobInput` (Id 25), and `RoutedAgentLaunchPlan` (Id 22); `AgentJobGrain.BuildDispatchAsync` writes `with["reasoningEffort"]` only when non-empty; `WorkflowItemTranslator` forwards `vars.agent.reasoningEffort` into `mohist/agent` dispatch options; the Runner plumbs `reasoningEffort` through `session-target.ts`, `followup-handler.ts` options, and `agent-job-executor.ts` (`readOptionalString`) into both turn executors. Later Agent edits, Agent deletion, or catalog changes never rewrite a frozen snapshot.
acceptanceCriteria: Every durable snapshot — `AgentJobInput`, `RoutedAgentLaunchPlan`, the `WorkDispatch` `with` payload, `AgentExecutionDefinition`, and runner session-target/follow-up definitions — carries the resolved effort beside model and variant, on manual HTTP, subscription/routed, mention, and workflow-task launch paths.
The dispatch `with` payload delivers the effort to the Runner, which reads it from the frozen payload and never re-reads the Agent definition to obtain it.
Editing the Agent's effort to `low` or deleting the Agent after a job was prepared with effort `high` leaves the in-flight job executing with the frozen `high`.
Append-only Orleans record conventions are respected: existing ids are unchanged, new fields use the design-assigned ids and deserialize when absent.

Runner executor tests cover payload plumbing into session-target, follow-up, and both turn executors, including absent effort; Server tests cover snapshot freezing on every launch path and immutability under Agent edit/delete.
Relevant Server and Runner tests and `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Effort resolution and append-only freezing across all server snapshot records, dispatch payload delivery, runner options/executor plumbing, and passing freezing/plumbing tests.
tasks.notes: Design D2. Do not pack effort into the variant string — one more frozen member of the same tuple. The capabilityRevision field of the tuple is added by T-006 when the expectation protocol lands; this task freezes the four data members.

tasks.title: Versioned runtime catalog entries separating true variants from reasoning efforts
tasks.description: Extend the catalog wire contract append-only: `RuntimeCatalogEntry` on `IRunnerGrain.cs` (Orleans Ids 2–5) and the Runner's `core/types.ts` gain per-model `ReasoningEfforts`, `SupportsReasoningEffort`, `Complete`, and a content-derived `CapabilityRevision`; old runners omitting the fields deserialize fine on the Server. In `runtime/host.ts registrationState()`, Pi publishes its native thinking levels under `reasoningEfforts` with `supportsReasoningEffort: true`, `complete: true` only once the catalog has loaded, and an empty true-variant map — thinking levels stop appearing as variants; OpenCode registers `supportsReasoningEffort: false` with its true variants unchanged and no efforts. `RunnerRoutes`/`RunnerRegistryGrain` store the entry verbatim in `RunnerInfo.RuntimeCatalogs`, and the Web settings/runner model-metadata queries expose `reasoningEfforts` through the existing plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: Pi registration publishes each model's thinking levels under `reasoningEfforts` and its `variants` map contains no thinking level; OpenCode reports `supportsReasoningEffort=false`, preserves its true variants, and publishes no reasoning efforts.

`capabilityRevision` is derived from catalog content so an identical re-registration (runner restart/reconnect) keeps the same revision, while a real capability change produces a new immutable revision; earlier revisions remain identifiable in stored snapshots.

`complete` is reported true only once the runtime's catalog has actually loaded; a catalog entry without `Complete` and `CapabilityRevision` round-trips as non-authoritative (fields absent) rather than crashing old or new readers.
The Server stores entries verbatim in `RunnerInfo.RuntimeCatalogs` and the Web settings/runner model-metadata queries expose per-model `reasoningEfforts` alongside variants.

Runner tests cover Pi and OpenCode registration shapes, revision stability across identical re-registration, new revision on capability change, and complete-only-after-load; Server tests cover append-only deserialization of legacy entries and verbatim storage; relevant tests pass.
tasks.output: Append-only capability fields on both sides of the catalog wire, honest Pi/OpenCode registration with the variant/effort split, content-derived capability revisions, verbatim server storage, Web metadata exposure, and passing registration/wire tests.
tasks.notes: Design D3. This lands the catalog half of the Pi variant/thinking-level break (levels no longer published as variants); the adapter half is T-004 and the explicit rejection is T-006. Confirm the content-hash revision is stable across serialization order on both sides before freeze (open question in design).

tasks.title: Native effort translation inside runtime adapters; delete the Pi variant/thinking-level smuggling
tasks.description: Remove the variant→thinking-level application in `runtime/pi/runtime.ts` (both sites) and add private `mapThinkingLevel(options.reasoningEffort)` applied via `session.setThinkingLevel`, including the session-reuse carry-over path; the applied effort flows into the projector's `model_change`/resolved-model payload as `appliedReasoningEffort` only when an effort was frozen. `runtime/opencode/runtime.ts` fails an explicit `reasoningEffort` in dispatch options with category `unsupported_execution_configuration` — never appending it to the model id, writing it to the variant, or silently ignoring it. No runtime ever receives another runtime's native value.
acceptanceCriteria: A supported Pi tuple with effort `high` and no variant maps `high` to Pi's native thinking level privately, and the execution evidence reports the applied effort.

A Pi dispatch carrying a variant but no effort never applies the variant to the thinking-level input; the old `if (options?.variant) session.setThinkingLevel(...)` paths are gone, and reused sessions carry over the effort-derived thinking level instead of a variant-derived one.
An OpenCode dispatch carrying an explicit reasoning effort fails with the `unsupported_execution_configuration` category; the effort never reaches the model id, variant, or is silently dropped.
A Pi-native thinking-level name never appears in any non-Pi adapter's model, variant, or effort fields (cross-runtime guard).
Absent effort is never synthesized into a default thinking level on any path.

Runner tests cover Pi effort→thinking-level mapping, variant-never-touches-thinking-level (including session reuse/carry-over), `appliedReasoningEffort` projection, and OpenCode explicit-effort rejection; relevant Runner tests and `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Pi adapter applying canonical effort as a private thinking level with applied-effort projection, removed variant smuggling, OpenCode explicit-effort failure, and passing adapter tests.
tasks.notes: Design D6 plus the adapter half of the Pi break. Keep the canonical→native mapping a private module function so Pi may diverge without a wire change. Saved Pi thinking-level variants become inert here; they become explicit deterministic rejections once T-006's resolver gates admission — the full 'removed with no compatibility layer' requirement is jointly met by T-003 + T-004 + T-006 with no migration, aliasing, or reinterpretation of stored data.

tasks.title: Pure server-side capability resolver with five typed dispositions
tasks.description: Add `Agent/Services/AgentExecutionCapabilityResolver` as a pure function over `(runtime, model, reasoningEffort, variant, catalog snapshot)` returning exactly one disposition — `supported` (with compatible runner identity), `needs-setup`, `unavailable`, `unsupported_execution_configuration`, `incompatible_execution_configuration` — per the design decision table. It mutates no owner state, claims no work, and executes nothing; explicit rejections are deterministic and unset effort imposes no requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: A complete catalog revision listing the tuple's model, effort, and variant returns `supported` with the compatible runner identity.
An absent, incomplete, or revision-less catalog entry returns `needs-setup` (non-terminal); a known-but-not-ready runtime returns `unavailable` (pending).

`supportsReasoningEffort=false` plus an explicit effort returns `unsupported_execution_configuration`; a complete catalog explicitly lacking the tuple's model, effort, or variant returns `incompatible_execution_configuration` with the frozen tuple preserved in the failure evidence.
An unset effort on an effort-unsupported runtime produces no rejection.

Re-evaluating the same tuple against the same catalog reproduces the same disposition (determinism), and the resolver performs no grain writes, claims, or execution (enforced by its pure signature and tests).

Unit tests cover the full decision table — every disposition, every scenario in the spec requirement, legacy non-authoritative entries, determinism, and the unset-effort exemption; relevant Server tests pass.
tasks.output: Pure AgentExecutionCapabilityResolver implementing the five-disposition decision table with runner identity on supported, and passing decision-table unit tests.
tasks.notes: Design D4. A missing catalog must stay `needs-setup`, never `incompatible` — a transient registration gap must not become a terminal user error. Consumed by T-006's admission path on the same runner catalog snapshot that produces the dispatch.

tasks.title: Resolver-gated admission with the conditional-claim capability fence and deterministic preflight failures
tasks.description: Wire the capability fence from the prerequisite design: `AgentJob` gains a read-only pending-dispatch projection and a conditional claim that persists the capability revision with the ledger dispatch snapshot before claim-visibility; Workflow exposes a read-only next-work projection with a stable pending work id that `DispatchService` translates into a conditional claim. `IRunnerGrain.TryClaimAgentJobAsync`/`TryClaimWorkflowAsync` accept the immutable expectation (frozen tuple + capability revision + generations) and compare it against the grain's current `RunnerInfo` catalog under `_lifecycleGate`. `DispatchService.AddPendingDispatchesAsync` runs the T-005 resolver before the claim on the same runner catalog snapshot that produces the dispatch; only `supported` is admitted; the Runner validates incoming dispatch snapshots against its current `capabilityRevision` and deterministically rejects stale ones (re-pending the work). Explicit rejections become preflight failures carrying the frozen tuple, with `unsupported_execution_configuration`/`incompatible_execution_configuration` registered as EventCatalog failure categories.
acceptanceCriteria: Only a `supported` disposition is admitted; `needs-setup` and `unavailable` skip the candidate without recording any failure, leaving the work pending — an absent or incomplete catalog never produces a dispatch or a terminal failure.

An explicit `unsupported_execution_configuration` or `incompatible_execution_configuration` disposition fails the work as a deterministic preflight failure carrying the frozen tuple and a matching EventCatalog failure category; re-evaluating the same tuple against the same catalog reproduces the same disposition.

A claim whose expectation matches the runner's current catalog revision is granted and the dispatch delivered; a re-registered catalog that no longer lists the frozen tuple refuses the claim and the work stays pending for re-resolution — the comparison happens under `_lifecycleGate` so heartbeat catalog repair cannot race the claim.

A dispatch snapshot frozen at revision R arriving at a runner whose current revision differs is rejected deterministically without execution, and the work is re-pended rather than silently executed with changed capability semantics.

The AgentJob conditional claim persists the capability revision with the ledger dispatch snapshot before the work becomes claim-visible, and `StoreActiveWorkDispatchAsync` remains the durable first-writer snapshot for Workflow claims.
The saved-Pi-thinking-level-variant scenario fails explicitly at preflight with the frozen tuple recorded — never applied as a thinking level, never silently dropped, with no migration or aliasing.

Server tests cover the fence (matching vs changed catalog, lifecycle-gate race), pending-on-absent-catalog, deterministic preflight failure with the frozen tuple, and both AgentJob and Workflow conditional-claim paths; Runner tests cover stale-snapshot rejection and re-pending; relevant tests pass.
tasks.output: Conditional AgentJob/Workflow claims with immutable capability expectations, resolver-gated admission on a single catalog snapshot, runner-side stale-snapshot rejection, preflight failure categories with frozen tuples, and passing fence/admission tests.
tasks.notes: Design D5, also satisfying 'Only supported tuples are admitted'. Resolution and claim must observe the same catalog snapshot. Decide the open question on non-Agent workflow tasks (`mohist/pi`/`mohist/opencode` actions): freeze the tuple with unset effort for uniformity unless implementation shows an exemption is required — record the decision in the code. Mixed-version fleets degrade safely to `needs-setup`.

tasks.title: Agent Readiness and execution evidence surface the effort
tasks.description: Extend `AgentReadinessService`: `MatchesCurrentDefinition` compares the resolved reasoning effort beside model/variant; `StructuralGaps` reports an actionable `effort-without-model` setup gap; `IsConfigurationFailure` classifies `unsupported_execution_configuration` and `incompatible_execution_configuration` (normalized `_`→`-`) as Needs setup with guidance to update the Agent's execution configuration. Execution evidence records the applied effort: session model facts record the adapter-reported `appliedReasoningEffort` distinct from model and variant, and the AgentJob terminal result carries the frozen effort beside model and variant; absent effort is recorded as absent, never synthesized.
acceptanceCriteria: An execution that ran with effort `high` no longer matches the current definition when the Agent defines effort `low` (and vice versa); matching executions require equal resolved effort.
An Agent with `reasoningEffort` set but no model yields a Needs-setup gap with actionable guidance naming the problem.
A latest execution failed with category `unsupported_execution_configuration` or `incompatible_execution_configuration` yields Needs setup with guidance to update the Agent's execution configuration.
A turn completing with frozen effort `high` records `high` as the applied effort in the session model facts and the AgentJob terminal output carries the effort beside model and variant.
A turn completing without a frozen effort records the effort as absent — no default value is synthesized anywhere in the evidence chain.

Server tests cover readiness definition-matching with effort, the effort-without-model gap, configuration-failure classification, and evidence recording (applied vs absent); relevant Server tests pass.
tasks.output: Effort-aware readiness matching, structural and failure-classification gaps, applied-effort evidence in session facts and AgentJob terminal results, and passing readiness/evidence tests.
tasks.notes: Design D7 + the readiness/evidence half of D8, also satisfying 'Execution evidence records the applied effort'. Readiness failure messages should tell the user exactly which key to re-enter (`reasoningEffort`) — the escape hatch for saved Pi thinking-level variants.

tasks.title: Web effort control and readiness display; runtime docs; end-to-end spec verification
tasks.description: Give `AgentProfileEditor` a reasoning-effort control separate from the variant control, driven by the selected runtime/model's catalog `reasoningEfforts` (via the T-003 settings/runner model-metadata queries) — never by the `variants` map; `model-variants.ts`/`ModelOptionList` keep serving true variants only. A selection with no `reasoningEfforts` or `supportsReasoningEffort=false` renders no effort options and saves no effort for that selection; readiness display surfaces effort gaps from T-007. Update `design/runtimes/pi.md` (effort maps to a thinking level, variant no longer does), `design/runtimes/opencode.md` (effort-unsupported contract), and the Agent-configuration user docs. Own the final cross-slice verification of both capability specs' scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: The effort control offers exactly the selected model's catalog `reasoningEfforts` and offers nothing from the `variants` map; selecting effort `high` saves `agentConfig.reasoningEffort: high` and leaves any `variant` value unchanged.
For a selection reporting no `reasoningEfforts` or `supportsReasoningEffort=false`, the control renders no effort values and cannot save an effort for that selection.
The Web readiness display surfaces effort setup gaps (effort-without-model, execution-configuration failures) with actionable guidance.

`design/runtimes/pi.md`, `design/runtimes/opencode.md`, and the Agent-configuration user docs describe the effort vocabulary, the removed Pi variant semantics, and the re-entry path for saved thinking-level variants.

Spec/system tests cover both capability specs' scenarios end-to-end: pending on absent catalog, explicit rejection recorded with the frozen tuple, snapshot immutability, Pi effort application with recorded evidence, OpenCode explicit failure, and no-migration behavior.
Web unit tests cover the effort control's catalog-driven options and no-support rendering; `npm run test:fast` and the full `npm run verify` gate pass.
tasks.output: Catalog-driven Web effort control and readiness surfacing, updated runtime/user docs, end-to-end spec verification, and a passing full repository verification gate.
tasks.notes: Design D8 (Web + docs) and D9 (spec/system coverage); this final coordinated slice owns `npm run verify`. The issue-level override UI stays Agent-profile-only in this change (per-launch UX is issue 556); the issue write surface itself already accepts the key from T-001.
